proposed.why: The evidence shows the provider returning 500s and payments-api's circuit breaker then opening. I can't see inside the provider, so I'm diagnosing now with moderate confidence.

diagnosis.hypothesis: fake-provider (the outside provider) began answering POST /v1/payments with HTTP 500 from about 08:25. payments-api retried each payment up to 3 times with backoff, which made requests slow. When the failures piled up, its provider circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on) opened. Since then payments-api rejects every POST /payments with 503 without calling the provider, and leaves the payment pending. That produces the 96% 5xx rate. The earlier retries explain the p95 latency above 2 s. The breaker is working as designed, so the root cause is the provider's 500s. Why the provider fails is not shown: there are no provider logs, and it looks healthy with 0 restarts. The slow-then-fast latency in the trace fits retries first and fast rejection afterwards.

evidence.shows: POST /payments 503s rose from about 0.04/s at 08:25 to 8.3/s at 08:26:49, while 201s fell to 0.28/s. This confirms the alert's symptom.
payments-api logs: 'provider unavailable; payment left pending', with the error '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open (next trial call in ~6-7 s)'. The 503s come from the open breaker.
Calls from payments-api to the provider returned 500s (up to about 0.48/s) next to 200s from 08:25. Provider calls drop to 0 by 08:26:56, which fits the breaker blocking calls.

A trace at 08:24:46 shows 3 provider POSTs to fake-provider /v1/payments, all HTTP 500, spaced about 200 ms and 400 ms apart. The request took 617 ms and ended in 503. This shows the provider failing and the client retrying.
fake-provider is running and healthy with 0 restarts, so the fault is not a crash. Its health check does not rule out failing payment handling.

Every container was recreated together at 08:24:32 with no per-service change. Settings are PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents and REFUND_CONNECTION=returned. Nothing shows one of our services being deployed with a bad setting, so a rollback is not clearly indicated.

proposed_fix.summary: Escalate to the provider and ask why POST /v1/payments is returning 500 since about 08:25. Keep the breaker on. It will close by itself once the provider recovers, because it probes with trial calls. Afterwards, find the payments left pending (e.g. pmt_000363 to pmt_000390 and later) and re-submit or reconcile them, then run money_check to confirm the books match the provider. Also check that the breaker's open threshold was not too sensitive, since 500s were only a small share of calls (c4).

diagnosis.blast_radius: No automated action is proposed. rollback_deploy only acts on our four services and would not fix a provider fault. Rolling back payments-api would restart it and could disable the breaker, which would send traffic to a failing provider. Payments left pending still need follow-up.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing is changed by this diagnosis, so there is nothing to undo. If the follow-up re-submission causes problems, stop it and rely on the idempotency keys to avoid double charges.
